To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
reversible flash-cooling can be used for the optimization of cryosolutions and for increasing X-ray resolution.

(i) the diffraction quality of crystals can be improved by changing the cryosolution concentration and (ii) the optimal cryosolution concentrations for flash-cooled pyrophosphatases are 0.5 M Na2SO4 and 0.2 M K2HPO4.

the resolution limit of flash-cooled crystals of Eschericia coli inorganic pyrrophosphatase was improved by almost 0,7 A, from about 1.8 A to about 1.15 Å, by using reversible flash-cooling in combination with concentration screening.

the development of methods for the preparation of cryosolutions for flash-cooling experiments.
the development of a new approach for optimizing the conditions for X-ray diffraction data collection at cryotemperature.

the use of reversible flash-cooling in combination with concentration screening of cryosolution components is an effective method to improve X-ray diffraction data quality.
